# iliad-022 — new renderings (Iliad 4.85–182)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Λυκηγενής (Ἀπόλλωνι Λυκηγενέϊ, 4.101, 4.119) | "Lycia-born" | "the Lycia-born" (+ note: sense not certain; "wolf-born", "light-born" proposed) | "wolf-born", "light-born" (each decides the dispute), "Lycegenes" (leaves the word untranslated); γίγνομαι "be born" |
| κλυτότοξος (4.101, 4.119) | "famed for the bow" | "famed for the bow" | "famous archer", "of the famous bow"; κλυτός "famous" as in κλυτοτέχνης "famous in craft" (1.571) |
| ἑκατόμβη · ῥέξειν ἑκατόμβην (4.102, 4.120) | "a famous hecatomb" · "sacrifice" | "a famous hecatomb" · "sacrifice" | "perform a hecatomb" (ῥέζω of sacrifice is "sacrifice", 2.400), "splendid", "glorious"; κλειτός = κλυτός "famous"; the note says a hecatomb is properly a hundred oxen |
| ἀρνῶν πρωτογόνων (4.102) | "of first-born lambs" | "of first-born lambs" | "firstling lambs", "first-born of the flock"; ἀρήν "lamb" (2.106), πρωτόγονος "first-born" |
| Ζελείης ἱερῆς (4.103) | "sacred Zeleia" | "sacred Zeleia" | "holy Zeleia" (reserved for ἠγάθεος); ἱερός "sacred" as in ἱερὴν πόλιν (1.366); Zeleia kept as a name, with the note saying it is Pandarus’ home town |
| ὣς φάτ’ … τῷ δὲ φρένας ἄφρονι πεῖθεν (4.104) | "the wits of him, senseless, she was persuading" | "she persuaded the wits of the senseless man" | "she won over the fool", "persuaded his foolish heart"; ἄφρων "senseless" (odyssey-035, iliad-018), φρένες "wits", πείθω "persuade" |
| ἐσύλα · σύλα πῶμα (4.105, 4.116) | "stripped" · "took the lid off" | "bared" · "took the lid off" | "unsheathed" (adds a sheath), "took the cover off" (adds a cover); συλάω is "strip, take off" and the object decides the English |
| ἐΰξοον (τόξον, 4.105) | "well-polished" | "well-polished" | "well-planed", "smooth"; follows the table’s ἐΰξοον ἅρμα "well-polished" (2.390) |
| ἰξάλου αἰγὸς ἀγρίου (4.105–106) | "of a bounding wild goat" | "of a bounding wild goat" (+ note: sense of ἴξαλος not certain) | "leaping", "ibex" (a species the Greek does not name), "agile"; "bounding" is the usual explanation |
| προδοκῇσι (4.107) | "ambush-places" | "in ambush" | "lurking-places", "hiding places", "blinds"; plural of a rare noun |
| ἑκκαιδεκάδωρα (4.109) | "sixteen-palm-long" | "sixteen palms long" (+ note: δῶρον "palm", a hand’s breadth) | "sixteen-handbreadths long", "of sixteen gifts" (the other δῶρον); δῶρον "gift" is kept for 4.97 |
| κεραοξόος τέκτων (4.110) | "a horn-polishing craftsman" | "a craftsman who polishes horn" | "horn-worker", "horn-smith"; κέρας "horn" + ξέω "scrape smooth, polish" |
| χρυσέην κορώνην (4.111) | "a golden tip" | "a golden tip" (+ note: κορώνη "crow", a curved end-piece) | "golden hook", "golden crow" (misleading), "golden ring"; the usual explanation is the curved end of the bow |
| τανυσσάμενος (4.112) | "having stretched it" | "strung" | "bent", "tensioned"; τανύω "stretch", which of a bow means "string" (Odyssey: "stretch bows") |
| σάκεα σχέθον ἐσθλοὶ ἑταῖροι (4.113) | "held their shields" … "the good companions" | "held up their shields" … "his good companions" | "stood shielding him", "formed a screen"; ἑταῖροι keeps the Odyssey’s "companions" |
| ἀβλῆτα (4.117) | "unshot" | "that had never been shot" | "unused", "new", "untried"; ἀ- + βάλλω |
| ἕρμα … μελαινέων ὀδυνάων (4.117) | "the prop of black pains" | "the prop of black pains" (+ note: figurative, sense not certain) | "the source of dark agony", "the foundation of black pains" (each decides the figure); ἕρμα keeps "props" (1.486), ὀδύνη the Odyssey’s "pains" (odyssey-005), μέλας "black" |
| πικρὸν ὀϊστόν (4.118, 4.134) | "the bitter arrow" | "the bitter arrow" | "sharp arrow" (reserved for ἐχεπευκής "sharp"), "cruel arrow", "keen"; πικρός "bitter" |
| κατεκόσμει (4.118) | "was setting in order" | "fitted" | "notched", "set", "arranged"; κοσμέω "set in order" (2.554) |
| γλυφίδας · νεῦρα βόεια (4.122) | "the notches" · "the ox-sinews" | "the nock" · "the ox-sinew string" | "the string-nick", "the oxhide string" (βόειος is "of ox" and νεῦρον "sinew"), "the arrow’s butt"; the plurals stand for one notch and one string |
| μαζῷ · σίδηρον (4.123) | "to his breast" · "the iron" | "to his breast" · "the iron" | "chest", "nipple" (μαζός); "the arrowhead" (σίδηρος stands for it, and the note says so) |
| κυκλοτερές (4.124) | "into a circle" | "into a circle" | "round", "in a ring", "into a curve"; adverb of κύκλος |
| λίγξε · ἴαχεν (4.125) | "twanged" · "cried out loudly" | "twanged" · "rang out loudly" | "sang", "hummed" (the Odyssey’s ἄεισε of a bowstring, 21.411); λίγγω-type verb, ἰάχω "cry out" |
| ὀξυβελής (4.126) | "sharp-shafted" | "sharp-pointed" | "keen-edged"; `l` "sharp-pointed" is kept for ἐχεπευκής (1.51), so ὀξύς "sharp" + βέλος "shaft" is made literal in `l`; `i` "sharp-pointed" is not the table’s `i` for ἐχεπευκής ("sharp") |
| ἀγελείη (Διὸς θυγάτηρ, 4.128) | "the daughter of Zeus, the spoil-driver" | "the daughter of Zeus, the driver of spoil" (+ note: sense uncertain) | follows the Odyssey table’s row (13.359), unchanged |
| βέλος ἐχεπευκές … ἄμυνεν (4.129) | "the sharp-pointed shaft" · "warded off" | "the sharp shaft" · "warded off" | "keen", "pointed"; follows 1.51 (`l` "sharp-pointed", `i` "sharp") and the table’s ἀμύνω "ward off" |
| ὡς ὅτε μήτηρ παιδὸς ἐέργῃ μυῖαν (4.130–131) | "as when a mother keeps a fly from her child" | "as a mother keeps a fly off her child" | "brushes away", "shoos"; εἴργω "keep off, shut out" |
| ὀχῆες χρύσειοι (4.132–133) | "the golden clasps" | "the golden clasps" | "bolts", "hooks", "fastenings"; ὀχεύς "holder, fastening"; χρύσεος "golden" |
| διπλόος θώρηξ (4.133) | "the double breastplate" | "the double breastplate" | "doubled", "two-fold corselet"; θώραξ keeps "breastplate" (3.332) and the Odyssey’s δίπλαξ "double" |
| ζωστῆρι ἀρηρότι (4.134) | "the fitted belt" | "the close-fitting belt" | "tight", "firm", "strongly fastened"; ἀραρίσκω "fit", as in ἀραρυίας "fitted" (3.331) |
| δαιδαλέοιο (ζωστῆρος, 4.135) | "wrought" | "finely wrought" | "cunning", "ornate", "intricate" (reserved for ποικίλος); the Odyssey’s δαιδαλέοισι θρόνοις "wrought chairs" / "finely wrought chairs" (odyssey-082); πολυδαίδαλος stays "much-wrought" / "richly wrought" |
| μίτρη (μίτρης, 4.137) | "the belly-guard" | "the belly-guard" (+ note: a metal guard for the lower body, worn under the belt; the usual explanation) | "mitre" (a bishop’s hat in English), "apron", "girdle-plate", "waist-guard"; ἔρυμα "protection" and ἕρκος "fence" say its use |
| ἔρυμα χροὸς ἕρκος ἀκόντων (4.137) | "protection of his skin, a fence against javelins" | "protection for his skin, a bulwark against javelins" | "defence", "guard" (kept for μίτρη); ἕρκος keeps the table’s "fence" in `l` and "bulwark" in `i` (1.283–284), ἄκων "javelin" |
| διὰ πρὸ δὲ εἴσατο (4.138) | "clean through … it sped" | "sped straight through" | "pierced" (drops εἴσατο), "drove straight through" (the Odyssey’s `i` for διαπρὸ δὲ εἴσατο χαλκός, odyssey-119); ἵεμαι "rush, speed" |
| ἐπέγραψε (4.139) | "grazed" (the line: "the topmost skin of the man the arrow grazed") | "grazed" | "scratched", "scored"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐπέγραψεν "grazed" (odyssey-108) |
| αἷμα κελαινεφές (4.140) | "dark-clouded" | "dark as a cloud" | "black-clouded", "cloud-dark"; follows the Odyssey’s κελαινεφὲς αἷμα (odyssey-051, odyssey-052) |
| φοίνικι μιήνῃ · μιάνθην (4.141, 4.146) | "stains with crimson" · "were stained" | "stains with crimson" · "were stained" | "dyes", "colours"; μιαίνω keeps the same word for dye and blood; φοῖνιξ "crimson" as at odyssey-113 |
| Μῃονίς · Κάειρα (4.142) | "a Maeonian woman" · "a Carian woman" | same (+ note: Maeonia is Lydia) | "Lydian", "from Asia Minor"; names kept as names |
| παρήϊον ἵππων (4.142) | "a cheek-piece for horses" | "a cheek-piece for horses" | "bridle-piece", "horse-harness", "jaw-guard"; παρήϊον "cheek-piece" in LSJ |
| θάλαμος (ἐν θαλάμῳ, 4.143) | "a chamber" | "a chamber" | "store-room", "bedchamber", "treasury"; follows the Odyssey’s θάλαμος "chamber" (odyssey-082) |
| ἠρήσαντο … φορέειν (4.143–144) | "have prayed to carry" | "have prayed to carry" | "have wished to wear" (decides the object), "begged", "vowed"; ἀράομαι "pray" |
| ἄγαλμα (βασιλῆϊ … ἄγαλμα, 4.144) | "a treasure" | "a treasure" | "a glory" (the Odyssey’s `l`, odyssey-019, 4.601; here κῦδος "glory" follows in 145), "an ornament" (the Odyssey’s `i`; here κόσμος "ornament" follows), "a delight"; a departure from the Odyssey with the reason |
| κόσμος (ἵππῳ κόσμος, 4.145) | "an ornament" | "an ornament" | "adornment", "order" (the Odyssey’s κόσμος "order", 8.489, a different sense), "decoration"; a departure from the Odyssey’s sense with the reason |
| ἐλατήρ (4.145) | "the driver" | "the man who drives it" | "charioteer", "rider"; ἐλαύνω "drive" |
| εὐφυέες (μηροί, 4.147) | "shapely" | "shapely" | "well-formed", "well-grown", "fine"; εὖ + φυή "growth, form" |
| σφυρὰ κάλ’ (4.147) | "the fair ankles" | "the fair ankles" | "beautiful", "fine"; καλός keeps the table’s "fair" for the body |
| νεῦρον · ὄγκοι (4.151) | "the sinew" · "the barbs" | "the sinew" · "the barbs" (+ note: usual explanation) | "the cord", "the binding", "the hooks"; ὄγκος "barb" is the usual explanation |
| ἄψορρον … θυμὸς ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀγέρθη (4.152) | "back again for him the heart in his chest was gathered" | "his heart came back together in his chest" | "his courage returned", "his spirit revived"; ἀγείρω "gather" |
| τοῖς δὲ βαρὺ στενάχων μετέφη κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων (4.153) | "And among them, groaning heavily, spoke lord Agamemnon," | "And among them lord Agamemnon spoke, groaning heavily," | "addressed them", "spoke to them"; βαρὺ στενάχων "groaning heavily" (1.364), κρείων "lord" (1.130), μετέφη "spoke among" |
| ἐπεστενάχοντο (4.154) | "groaned along" | "joined in his groaning" | "groaned in answer" (decides response), "sighed"; ἐπιστενάχομαι "groan in addition" |
| ὅρκι’ ἔταμνον (4.155) | "the oaths I was cutting" | "I was making the oaths" | "I was swearing", "I was striking a treaty"; τάμνω "cut" as in ὅρκια ταμόντες (2.124) |
| προστήσας (4.156) | "setting forward" | "set out" | "putting in front", "placing as champion"; προΐστημι "set before" |
| ὥς σ’ ἔβαλον Τρῶες (4.157) | "so the Trojans have struck you" | "And so the Trojans have hit you" (+ note: ὥς "so", could be "since") | "since", "now that" (each decides the open reading); βάλλω "hit" |
| ἅλιον ὅρκιον (4.158) | "vain is the oath" | "the oath is not vain" | "idle", "fruitless"; ἅλιος "vain" as at 4.26 (iliad-021) |
| ἀπέτισαν (4.161) | "paid back" | "pay" (gnomic aorist, said in the note) | "have paid", "paid dearly"; ἀποτίνω "pay back" |
| εἴ περ … ἔκ τε … τελεῖ (4.160–161) | "even if … yet even late he fulfils it" | "even if … he fulfils it late all the same" | "he brings it about", "completes"; τελέω keeps "fulfil" (1.5 Διὸς ἐτελείετο βουλή) |
| ἔσσεται ἦμαρ ὅτ’ ἄν ποτ’ ὀλώλῃ (4.164) | "there will be a day when at some time shall have perished" | "There will come a day when … will have perished" | "a day is coming", "the day will come"; ἦμαρ "day" |
| ὑψίζυγος (Ζεύς, 4.166) | "sitting on high" | "who sits on high" (+ note: ὕψι + ζυγόν "bench, seat") | "high-throned" (θρόνος is another word; "golden-throned" is χρυσόθρονος), "high-yoked", "on high" alone (loses ζυγόν) |
| ἐρεμνὴν αἰγίδα (4.167) | "the dusky aegis" | "the dusky aegis" | "black aegis", "dark aegis" (μέλας and ἐρεμνός are kept apart); follows the Odyssey’s ἐρεμνός "dusky" (11.606, 24.106) |
| ἐπισσείῃσιν (4.167) | "shall shake over" | "shall shake over" | "brandish", "wave"; σείω "shake" (3.345) |
| τῆσδ’ ἀπάτης κοτέων (4.168) | "bearing a grudge over this deceit" | "in resentment at this deceit" | "angry at" (χόλος), "in wrath" (μῆνις); κοτέω "bear a grudge" (1.181); ἀπάτη "deceit" (iliad-008) |
| αἰνὸν ἄχος (4.169) | "fearsome grief" | "fearsome grief" | "dread grief", "terrible grief"; αἰνός keeps "fearsome" as at φύλοπιν αἰνήν; ἄχος "grief" |
| πότμον ἀναπλήσῃς βιότοιο (4.170) | "fill up the doom of your life" | "fill up the doom of your life" | "fill the measure of your days" (adds), "complete your fate" (reserved for μοῖρα); πότμος keeps the Odyssey’s "doom" (ἀεικέα πότμον) |
| πολυδίψιον Ἄργος (4.171) | "much-thirsty Argos" | "very thirsty Argos" | "arid", "dry", "waterless"; πολύ- "much" + δίψα "thirst" |
| ἐλέγχιστος (4.171) | "most shameful" | "most shameful" | "most disgraced" (adds), "basest"; the shipped iliad-010 rendering of the same word |
| κὰδ … λίποιμεν (4.173) | "leave behind" | "leave behind" | "abandon", "give up"; καταλείπω with tmesis |
| ὀστέα πύσει ἄρουρα (4.174) | "the plough-land will rot your bones" | "the plough-land will rot your bones" | "the earth will rot", "the soil will consume"; ἄρουρα keeps "plough-land" (the Odyssey table) |
| ἀτελευτήτῳ ἐπὶ ἔργῳ (4.175) | "upon an unfulfilled task" | "with the task unfulfilled" | "unfinished", "unaccomplished" (reserved for ἀτέλεστος); keeps the table’s ἀτελεύτητον "unfulfilled" (1.527) |
| ὑπερηνορεόντων (Τρώων, 4.176) | "over-bold" | "overbearing" | "overweening" (reserved for ὑπερφίαλος), "arrogant"; follows the Odyssey table’s row for ὑπερηνορέοντες (6.5) |
| τύμβῳ ἐπιθρῴσκων (4.177) | "leaping upon the tomb" | "leaps upon the tomb" | "dancing on", "stamping on"; ἐπιθρῴσκω "leap upon", τύμβος "tomb" (iliad-013) |
| κυδαλίμοιο (Μενελάου, 4.100, 4.177) | "the glorious" | "glorious" | "renowned", "famed" (κλυτός), "noble"; follows the Odyssey’s κυδάλιμος "glorious" (odyssey-072) |
| αἴθ’ … τελέσει’ (4.178) | "Would that … might fulfil" | "If only … would fulfil" | "May he", "I wish"; αἴθε "would that" as in the table’s αἴθ’ ὄφελες |
| χόλον τελέσει’ (4.178) | "fulfil his anger" | "fulfil his anger" | "vent", "satisfy", "carry out"; τελέω "fulfil", χόλος "anger" |
| ἅλιον στρατὸν … ἤγαγεν (4.179) | "a vain army" | "led the army … here in vain" | "a useless host", "to no purpose" (reserved for αὔτως); ἅλιος "vain" |
| κεινῇσιν νηυσίν (4.181) | "with empty ships" | "with empty ships" | "with hollow ships" (κοῖλος), "with idle ships"; κενός "empty" (the table’s κενεόν "empty-handed") |
| χάνοι εὐρεῖα χθών (4.182) | "may the wide earth gape" | "may the wide earth open for me" | "swallow me", "may the earth swallow me up" (adds a verb), "yawn"; χάσκω "gape" |
